title: A Inheritance for the Alibi
premise: Mara Underhill, cathedral archivist and quiet solver of three 'accidental' deaths, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after a stranger's funeral — a letter naming her as sole heir to an estate she's never heard of. The letter claims the true killer is the same man the police cleared, and that a witness who can prove it is alive, hidden somewhere in the cathedral's locked crypt. As Mara investigates, she falls for Daniel Voss, the dead man's estranged son who arrives to contest the inheritance, unaware his father's letter implicates Daniel's own stepmother. In the crypt's sealed chamber they find the witness — a woman declared dead years ago, living in hiding — and Mara must choose between turning over evidence that will destroy the man she loves' family and letting a fourth death go unanswered. She chooses justice: the stepmother is exposed at the probate hearing, the inheritance passes to a hospice charity, and Mara and Daniel, bound by grief rather than blood, begin again together.
about_author: Elodie Crane spent a decade cataloguing parish records in northern England before turning to fiction, a career that taught her how much truth hides in filing cabinets. She writes mysteries about people who notice what institutions prefer to forget.

chapters.title: The Postmark Problem
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. While cataloguing funeral records, Mara receives a lawyer's letter containing a stranger's confession and naming her an heir — postmarked one day after the man's burial. The emotional beat is unease sharpening into obsession; she rereads the confession until midnight, unable to explain why a dying man chose her.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback-structured. We learn how she quietly unraveled three deaths the police closed as accidents, using archival habits of mind rather than detective training. The beat establishes her competence and her loneliness — solving deaths has cost her friendships and nearly her faith.

chapters.title: The Son Arrives
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel Voss storms into the cathedral to confront the stranger inheriting his father's estate, expecting a con artist and finding instead a careful archivist who knows more about his father's last weeks than he does. The beat is friction laced with reluctant fascination on both sides.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cross-referencing the confession against cathedral ledgers, Mara finds the dead man visited the archive four times in his final month, always asking about the locked crypt. The beat is the thrill of a pattern emerging — and the first hint someone else has been searching the same records before her.

chapters.title: A Witness, Deceased
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel shares that his father's business partner, Iris Calloway, died five years ago — the very witness the confession names. He shows Mara the death certificate, but Mara notices the certifying doctor was also the third 'accident.' The beat is dread: the paperwork of death can be manufactured.

chapters.title: The Stepmother's Grief
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the funeral reception's aftermath, Mara observes Vivian Voss, Daniel's stepmother, performing flawless mourning while steering every conversation away from the crypt. A small slip — she mentions a room she shouldn't know exists — plants the first seed of suspicion. Beat: polished surfaces hiding cracks.

chapters.title: Keys and Obligations
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel petitions the diocese to open the crypt and is refused; only the bishop holds the key, and the bishop owes Vivian's family old favors. Daniel's sense of duty to his father's memory collides with his growing loyalty to Mara. Beat: love beginning to complicate obligation.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The doctor who signed Iris Calloway's death certificate falls from the bell tower — ruled suicide. Mara finds his appointment book torn, but a pencil rubbing reveals his last meeting was with 'V.V.' The beat is cold fear: the killer is accelerating because Mara is close.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Cloister
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel confesses to Mara that he'd been estranged from his father for years over money, and that his absence let Vivian isolate the old man. Mara admits she almost didn't send the letter to police because part of her wanted to solve it alone. Beat: mutual vulnerability deepening into trust.

chapters.title: Sealed Since 1987
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging through restoration records, Mara learns the crypt was sealed after a fire in 1987 — the same year Iris Calloway supposedly died. A maintenance invoice shows someone paid for the seal personally: Vivian's first husband. Beat: the past and present locking together like tumblers.

chapters.title: Threats in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Someone ransacks the archive overnight, taking the 1987 restoration file, and leaves a warning scrawled in a psalter: some doors stay shut. Daniel insists Mara go to the police; she refuses, knowing their track record with her theories. Beat: the first real quarrel between them.

chapters.title: The Bishop's Debt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confronts the bishop gently, offering him a way out: she won't expose his financial entanglement with Vivian if he opens the crypt. He gives her three days. Beat: justice negotiated outside the law, Mara crossing a line she once drew firmly.

chapters.title: Below the Nave
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Daniel and Mara descend into the crypt by lamplight, finding it stripped of coffins except one unmarked slab — and signs someone has lived there: a cot, tinned food, a Bible annotated in a woman's hand. Beat: awe curdling into horror at what the church concealed.

chapters.title: Iris
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They find Iris Calloway alive, aged and half-blind, hiding in the crypt since faking her death to escape Vivian's husband's crimes — crimes she witnessed. She has the original ledger proving the inheritance fraud, but refuses to surface, terrified. Beat: the witness everyone swears is dead, found.

chapters.title: Vivian's Visit
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Vivian appears at the cathedral unexpectedly, probing Daniel about the crypt with maternal warmth that doesn't reach her eyes. She offers him his father's estate outright if the 'archivist matter' resolves quietly. Beat: temptation offered plainly, and Daniel understanding exactly what she means.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vivian corners Mara alone and lays it bare: the confession letter was meant for a solicitor who died before mailing it; Mara was never supposed to be heir or investigator. She offers money, then implies the bell tower. Beat: menace without violence, and Mara refusing anyway.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Iris vanishes from the crypt — taken or fled — leaving behind her annotated Bible open to a verse about resurrection. Daniel blames himself for telling Vivian's driver about the descent. Beat: despair, and the realization the killer now controls the timeline.

chapters.title: The Probate Hearing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With Iris missing and evidence thin, Mara gambles everything: she requests the probate hearing be held in the cathedral itself, then presents the confession, the ledger copy she'd secretly made, and the crypt's living quarters as exhibits. Beat: rising tension toward public exposure.

chapters.title: Resurrection
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. At the hearing's crisis point, Iris emerges from the nave shadows — Daniel had hidden her in the bell tower, gambling Vivian would move her and reveal herself. Confronted by the living witness, Vivian breaks and confesses to the doctor's murder and her husband's cover-up. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Stone
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Police finally believe her; the three old accidents are reopened and two confirmed murders. The bishop resigns quietly. Mara walks the empty cathedral feeling neither triumphant nor light — justice arrived, but late and costly. Beat: sober reckoning with what vigilance costs.

chapters.title: The Estate Settled
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. The inheritance passes to a hospice charity per the dead man's true wishes, which the confession reveals. Daniel and Iris reconcile over shared grief; Daniel declines the estate entirely. Beat: release — duty honored not through property but through truth.

chapters.title: A New Entry in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing chapter. Months later, Mara files the case among her private records and finds a new anonymous letter waiting — another death ruled accidental, another pattern. Daniel asks if she'll look into it; she takes his hand and says yes. Beat: love chosen alongside the work, and the door left open.
